T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach with a focus on user-friendly navigation and search functionality for problems.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for different screen sizes.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, update, and deletion.
T2.notes: Implement validation and error handling for API endpoints.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store problem details, tags, difficulty levels, and solutions.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a form-based interface for users to submit code with syntax highlighting and file upload support.
T4.notes: Include real-time validation for supported programming languages.

T5.implementation_approach: Use a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security by isolating execution environments.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, activity history, and achievements.
T6.notes: Incorporate editable fields for user information.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user data, including profile updates and retrieval.
T7.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user data.

T8.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display top users based on scores or activity.
T8.notes: Include sorting and filtering options for better usability.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data dynamically.
T9.notes: Optimize queries for real-time leaderboard updates.

T10.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and explanations for problems in a collapsible format.
T10.notes: Ensure hints are displayed progressively to avoid spoilers.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and explanations, including creation, retrieval, and updates.
T11.notes: Implement role-based access control for editing hints.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify problem library functionality.
T12.notes: Focus on edge cases and API response validation.

T13.implementation_approach: Simulate code submissions and evaluate the correctness of the evaluation system.
T13.notes: Test for security vulnerabilities in the code execution environment.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionalities, including data updates and retrieval.
T14.notes: Ensure proper handling of authentication and authorization.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify leaderboard accuracy and performance under high load.
T15.notes: Test for real-time updates and data consistency.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the functionality and accessibility of hints and explanations.
T16.notes: Ensure hints are displayed correctly and progressively.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using a CI/CD pipeline with containerization and cloud hosting.
T17.notes: Ensure proper monitoring and logging for the deployed application.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __init__(self, title, description, difficulty):
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title} (Difficulty: {self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), nullable=False, unique=True)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False, unique=True)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

    def set_password(self, password):
        # Add password hashing logic here if needed
        self.password_hash = password

    def check_password(self, password):
        # Add password hash verification logic here if needed
        return self.password_hash == password

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    submitted_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    status = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'Accepted', 'Wrong Answer', etc.

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} status={self.status}>"

files.content:
# app/routes.py
# Purpose: Aggregate all blueprints
# Layer: assembly

from app.controllers.problem_controller import blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

# List of all blueprints to be registered
blueprints = [
    problem_blueprint,
    user_blueprint,
    solution_blueprint
]

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the Flask application instance.
    
    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    for blueprint in blueprints:
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Register blueprints for modular route handling
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

    return app

from app import create_app

# Application entry point
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn effectively.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
